He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]], where he was a freshman member of their NCAA national championship team in [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2007]]. The [[Philadelphia 76ers]] selected Speights in the first round of the [[2008 NBA draft]] with the 16th overall pick. With the [[Golden State Warriors]], he won an [[NBA championship]] in 2015. ==Early life== Speights was born in [[St. Petersburg, Florida]]. He played basketball at St. Petersburg's [[Admiral Farragut Academy]], which retired his jersey number after one year.{{cite web |url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/2007/05/11/afa-honors-current-gator-speights/ |title=AFA Honors Current Gator Speights |website=TampaBay.com |date=May 11, 2007 |access-date=April 19, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220419125245/https://www.tampabay.com/archive/2007/05/11/afa-honors-current-gator-speights/ |archive-date=April 19, 2022}} He also played basketball at [[Hargrave Military Academy]] (senior year) and [[Gibbs High School (St. Petersburg, Florida)|Gibbs High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whiteja02.html|title= James White|publisher= Basketball-Reference.Com |access-date= November 15, 2012}} Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Speights was listed as the No. 13 power forward and the No. 51 player in the nation in 2006.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Marreese-Speights-33526;_ylt=AkDjBQDyHJwYGQ4sYWDt48lGPZB4|title=Rivals.com|website=sports.yahoo.com|access-date=July 7, 2017}} ==College career== [[File:Marreese Speights.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Speights (#34) in 2008]] Speights began his career at the [[University of Florida]] in [[2006–07 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2006–07]], and averaged approximately four points and two rebounds in six minutes per game as a freshman for the national champion [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Gators]]. He saw few minutes behind big men [[Al Horford]], [[Joakim Noah]], and [[Chris Richard (basketball)|Chris Richard]]. Speights ended the 2007–08 season averaging 14.5 points, 8.1 rebounds, and 1.4 blocks per game. After his sophomore season, he declared himself eligible for the [[2008 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/basketball/ncaa/wires/04/08/2060.ap.bkc.florida.speights.0160/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080412153735/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/basketball/ncaa/wires/04/08/2060.ap.bkc.florida.speights.0160/|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 12, 2008|title=Marreese Speights declares for NBA Draft|website=cnn.com|access-date=July 7, 2017}} Speights confirmed with Florida coach [[Billy Donovan]] on June 12, 2008, that he would not be returning to the Gators.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2008/news/story?id=3439407|title=Florida's Speights to keep name in NBA draft|date=June 12, 2008|website=ESPN.com|access-date=July 7, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2008–2012)=== Speights was drafted by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] with the 16th pick of the first round in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. He signed with Philadelphia on July 18, 2008.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers_sign_speights_080718.html?rss=true|title=SIXERS: 76ers Sign First Round Draft Pick Marreese Speights|website=www.nba.com|access-date=July 7, 2017}} As a rookie, Speights had a field-goal percentage of .502 from the field, playing 79 games, shooting .773 from the free throw line, and notching two starts. [[File:JaVale McGee and Marreese Speights.jpg|thumb|Speights (right) battling [[JaVale McGee]] in 2010|left]] Speights' second season with the 76ers started off on a high note, as he saw a slight increase in playing time and put up good numbers. Speights scored 15 or more points in five of his first 10 games and was a vital part of the team's frontcourt. During the fourth quarter of the November 14 game against the [[Chicago Bulls]], Speights injured his left knee. An MRI revealed a partial tear of his [[medial collateral ligament]] (MCL). Speights missed 14 games and came back December 16, to play 22 minutes in a losing effort against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. After returning from the injury, his playing time became limited, mostly because of the increased production from [[Elton Brand]]. The 76ers hired [[Doug Collins (basketball)|Doug Collins]] as their new head coach for the 2010–11 season. Known for his defensive-minded coaching philosophy, this shift in team focus adversely affected Speights, who was known more for his offensive capabilities. Frequent clashes with the coaching staff led to a career-low 11.5 minutes per contest. However, Speights got one start against the [[New Orleans Hornets]] on January 3, 2011, and notched 12 points and six rebounds. For the season, Speights averaged 5.4 points and 3.3 rebounds, both career lows. ===Memphis Grizzlies (2012–2013)=== On January 4, 2012, Speights was acquired by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] as a part of a three-team trade that sent [[Xavier Henry]] to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] and two future second round picks to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web | title = Grizzlies acquire Marreese Speights from 76ers | url = http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-marreese-speights-76ers | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = January 4, 2012 | access-date = January 4, 2012}} On June 29, 2012, the Grizzlies extended a qualifying offer to Speights, making him a restricted free agent.{{cite web | title = Grizzlies extend qualifying offers to Arthur and Speights | url = http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-extend-qualifying-offers-arthur-and-speights | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = June 29, 2012 | access-date = June 29, 2012}} However, on July 13, Speights re-signed with the Grizzlies to a two-year, $8 million contract.{{cite web | title = Grizzles sign Marreese Speights and Darrell Arthur to multi-year contracts | url = http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/arthur_speights_signed_multi_year_contracts-120713 | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = July 13, 2012 | access-date = January 22, 2013}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2013)=== [[File:Marreese Speights block.jpg|thumbnail|upright|Speights attempting to block a shot from [[Tony Allen (basketball)|Tony Allen]] in 2013]] On January 22, 2013, Speights was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], along with [[Wayne Ellington]], [[Josh Selby]], and a future first round draft pick, in exchange for [[Jon Leuer]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/trade-130122 | title=Cavaliers Acquire Speights, Ellington, Selby and Future First Round Pick From Grizzlies |work=NBA.com| date=January 22, 2013| access-date=January 22, 2013}} In his half a season with the Cavaliers, Speights averaged 10.2 points and 5.1 rebounds in 39 games. ===Golden State Warriors (2013–2016)=== On July 12, 2013, Speights signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/speights-signing-071213|title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Forward/center Marreese Speights to Contract|date=July 12, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 29, 2015}} On February 10, 2014, Speights scored a career-high 32 points in a 123–80 victory over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140210/PHIGSW/gameinfo.html|title=76ers at Warriors|website=nba.com|access-date=July 7, 2017}} Speights won his first NBA championship with the Warriors after they defeated the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2015 NBA Finals]] in six games. After being the team's top scoring option off the bench in 2014–15, Speights gained the nickname "Mo Buckets".{{cite web|url=http://www.csnbayarea.com/warriors/struggling-speights-mo-buckets-will-be-back-sure|title=Struggling Speights: 'Mo Buckets will be back for sure'|date=November 19, 2015|website=csnbayarea.com|access-date=July 7, 2017}} On June 29, 2015, the Warriors exercised his team option for the 2015–16 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-exercise-contract-option-forward-marreese-speights-2015-16-season|title=Warriors Exercise Contract Option on Forward Marreese Speights for 2015-16 Season|date=June 29, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 29, 2015}} During the 2015–16 season, Speights helped the Warriors record a 24–0 start to the season (an NBA record) and helped them finish 73–9, the best overall record in NBA history, surpassing the 1995–96 Chicago Bulls' mark of 72–10. In Game 3 of the Warriors' 2016 first-round playoff series against the Houston Rockets, Speights, who didn't attempt a three-pointer in the first 29 playoff games of his career, was 3-of-6 on three-pointers and finished with 22 points in a 97–96 loss.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160421/GSWHOU/gameinfo.html|title=Harden's late shot lifts Rockets over Warriors 97-96|date=April 21, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 22, 2016}} The Warriors went on to defeat the Rockets in five games. In the second round, Speights helped the Warriors defeat the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in five games to qualify for the Western Conference Finals. In their conference finals match-up with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], the Warriors fought back from a 3–1 deficit in the series to clinch a 4–3 victory. In Game 5 of the series, Speights scored 14 points in nine minutes to help the Warriors save their season. With a Game 7 victory, the Warriors moved on to the [[2016 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] for the second straight year, where they would again face the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. Despite the Warriors going up 3–1 in the series following a Game 4 victory, they went on to lose the series in seven games to become the first team in NBA history to lose the championship series after being up 3–1. ===Los Angeles Clippers (2016–2017)=== On July 12, 2016, Speights signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-marreese-speights|title=CLIPPERS SIGN MARREESE SPEIGHTS|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2016|access-date=July 12, 2016}} On January 16, 2017, he scored a season-high 23 points in a 120–98 victory over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900042|title=Paul hurt but Clippers trounce Thunder to go 7-0 in 2017|work=ESPN.com|date=January 16, 2016|access-date=January 17, 2017}} On May 23, Speights opted out of his contract for the 2017–18 season with the Clippers, making him an unrestricted free agent.{{cite web|last=Turner|first=Broderick|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/la-sp-clippers-speights-20170523-story.html|title=Marreese Speights opts out of his contract with Clippers; others may soon do the same|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=May 23, 2017|access-date=July 7, 2017}} ===Orlando Magic (2017–2018)=== On July 27, 2017, Speights signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-marreese-speights|title=Magic Sign Marreese Speights|work=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2017|access-date=July 27, 2017}} On October 30, he scored 18 points and hit a career-high six three-pointers, including five in a six-minute span, during a 115–99 victory over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974848|title=Speights' 3-point outburst leads Magic past Pelicans, 115-99|work=ESPN.com|date=October 30, 2017|access-date=October 30, 2017}} ===Guangzhou Loong Lions (2018–2021)=== On July 2, 2018, the [[Guangzhou Long-Lions|Guangzhou Loong Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]] announced the signing of Marreese Speights.{{cite web|title=官宣：斯贝茨正式加盟广州龙狮|language=ZH|url=http://www.longlions.com/index.php?c=article&id=902|date=July 2, 2018|website=longlions.com|access-date=July 2, 2018}}{{cite web the [[Guangzhou Long-Lions]] had re-signed Speights.{{cite web|title=Long Lions keep Speights for another season|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/641184/Long-Lions-keep-Speights-for-another-season|date=August 17, 2020|website=asia-basket.com|access-date=August 17, 2020}} ==Coaching career== On
